article.name: ArcRift
article.summary: ArcRift is a local-first AI memory application combining a browser extension, desktop dashboard, backend, and MCP server. It stores conversations and extracted graph facts by project/session, then retrieves vector, keyword, and graph context for browser prompts or coding agents. This pinned source review contains no runtime or benchmark results.

who_what.text: The official README credits ArcRift as built by Eshaan Nair and presents it as a self-hostable memory application for browser AI conversations and coding agents, with a browser extension, desktop dashboard, backend, and MCP server.

architecture.text: The documented architecture comprises a browser extension, a Tauri/React desktop interface, a Node.js backend, and an MCP stdio server. Storage adapters select SQLite/SQLite-vec or a Docker profile using MongoDB, Neo4j, and ChromaDB.

The SQLite schema separates sessions, full chats, background jobs, graph facts, chunk metadata, sentence metadata, vector tables, and FTS5. Facts carry typed subject/relation/object fields, session ID, and timestamp. Chunks carry session, chunk index, content, and optional file path/hash; vector dimensions are 768.

Browser ingestion scrubs PII and queues chat processing. The MCP store path separately writes a full chat, attempts graph extraction, creates vector chunks, then updates session counts. The MCP chunker call passes 150-word windows and 50-word overlap; the architecture guide describes 300/80 for the browser chat path.

behavior.text: Browser chat save validates its inputs, scrubs PII, enqueues a chat_ingestion job, and returns a job ID. MCP store_memory finds a session by ID or name, creates one if absent, saves the full chat, attempts to extract and save graph triples, stores vector chunks, and updates statistics. Graph extraction failure does not prevent the vector write.

Full chat saves use an upsert. Vector storage replaces chunk records. The inspected MCP tools expose prune-and-rewrite rather than a general versioned fact correction API; correction coverage and stale-value behavior were not measured.

MCP pruning derives entities from the request, falls back to long tokens if extraction fails, deletes matching graph facts by session, and deletes chunk text matching the query substring. SQLite session deletion removes vector rows and deletes the session with related metadata/facts/full chats. The HTTP chat DELETE path only calls vector deletion and does not call session deletion in the inspected code.

MCP recall extracts query entities, looks up up to 15 graph facts for the selected session, retrieves top-N vector chunks, sanitizes chunks, then renders both facts and context. SQLite vector retrieval combines sentence vectors, chunk vectors, and FTS; applies a 0.30 threshold, trims matched sentences, sorts, and caps results. Documentation describes browser hybrid retrieval and a deliberate global cross-project search path.

Session identifiers scope graph facts and chunk metadata on scoped paths. The explicit global search path omits a session filter. The boundary is session/project scope, not a user or organization identity. Store can fall back from ID to project name, while recall directly looks up its argument as a session ID; the deployed caller contract was not established.

Full chats retain text, platform, message count, and timestamps. Graph facts retain typed relations, session ID, and timestamp; chunks retain session/index/text and optional file path/hash. Recall debug output can name retrieval engines, but the inspected fact response does not provide claim-level source spans or citations.

metrics.evidence: Scoped graph/vector retrieval and thresholding are source-visible; no answerability fixture outcomes were collected.
Full-chat upsert and prune-and-rewrite are visible; no correction or stale-value probes were run.
SQLite cleanup paths are visible, alongside the narrower HTTP DELETE path; no residual-data audit was run.
Scoped paths filter by session ID and global search intentionally crosses sessions; no isolation or authorization probes were run.
Records contain session/time/type fields and chunks can retain source paths/hashes; no answer citation scoring was done.
Browser ingestion and sentence indexing use background jobs and retrieval uses bounded candidate limits; no timings were collected.
The README describes local Ollama and optional Groq use; no provider usage or token-cost instrumentation was measured.
The schema and storage adapters identify persistence structures; no attributable bytes or growth measurement was collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of selected docs and SQLite implementations, not an end-to-end runtime review. Runtime retrieval quality, model behavior, prompt-injection resistance, storage-mode parity, authorization, deletion completeness, and performance remain unverified.
The README and architecture guide mention benchmark values and isolation audits; this review did not reproduce or adjudicate them, and they are not results produced here.

benchmark.note: No ArcRift runtime, benchmark workload, build, or tests were run. Source observations and upstream project-reported claims are not measurements from this review.
